beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: A few weeks after saying yes, Riley's mid-rehearsal blitz with the new band.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "My old band asked if I'd come back instead. I already told them no — but first I want to look at the thing that actually got me on this tour in the first place."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for what's been growing this whole time.

options.text: Still alive, still taking shape — this hasn't stopped growing.
It means the songs were never that good to begin with.
The past growing doesn't affect anything now.

elaboration: The Empress doesn't stop once something's shared — abundance that comes from letting it flourish keeps compounding, it doesn't cash out in one moment.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. Now the thing that's actually happening to me right now."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You draw for where you actually stand right now.

options.text: Standing right at the edge — calm, not scared of the fall.
It means you jumped without looking.
This card has nothing to do with actually being on tour.

elaboration: The Fool isn't reckless — it's the one figure calm enough to see exactly where the edge is and step off it anyway.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Saying no to my old band felt like closing a door for good. Is that what this is?"

options.text: Exactly — one thing ending as another begins, in the same breath.
It means that door's actually still open.
Closing doors isn't something this card touches.

elaboration: Beginning and ending in one — the Fool doesn't wait for the old door to fully shut before the new one opens. They happen together.
